paper_title: Stellar Basins of Gravitationally Bound Particles
notes: Paper presents NEW exclusion limits on axion-electron coupling g_ae from the 'Solar basin' phenomenon—a novel accumulation of bound axions around the Sun. The main result (Fig. 3, blue region) recasts XENON1T dark-matter axion searches as coupling limits independent of dark-matter assumptions, using Eq. 28. Conservative limit (thin blue curve, Eq. 9) excludes g_ae ≳ 1.0e-13 for m ≳ 0.7 keV. The paper also identifies a potential signal region ('basin excess', green box) at m ∈ [1.5–3] keV where g_ae ∼ 2–3 × 10^-12 could explain the XENON1T excess if the optimistic ejection timescale (Eq. 11) is correct. Data points extracted from Fig. 3: conservative limit approximated as a horizontal line at g_ae ≈ 1.0e-13 spanning 0.1 eV to 100 eV (mass-independent over this range); signal region boundaries at m ≈ 0.7–3 keV and g_ae ≈ 2–3 × 10^-12. The coupling type is AxionElectron because the paper explicitly studies the pseudoscalar-electron coupling g_ae (Eq. 17: L ⊃ g_ae/(2m_e) (∂_μ a) ψ̄_e γ^μ γ^5 ψ_e). Confidence is 0.75 (not higher) because the paper's primary focus is on the novel basin phenomenon rather than a traditional exclusion-limit measurement, and the exact numerical limits depend on uncertain gravitational ejection timescales (Eqs. 9–11). | selector: text (sole candidate)
